newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia budget key to lower long term rates - PM.
newsitem.headline: Australia budget key to lower long term rates - PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday the budget deficit had to be cut if Australia wanted lower real interest rates in the long term.
"In the long run if you want to get interest rates down you get rid of budget deficits," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.
"People who criticise the removal of budget deficits are really arguing for much higher interest rates," he said.
"One of the reasons that we are paying much higher real interest rates in this country is that over the years we have have run up huge budget deficits," he said.
"And when you run up huge budget deficits people who lend you money from abroad charge a premium and that's one of the reasons why Peter Costello and I are cutting the budget deficit."
The Liberal-National government has said it expected to have an underlying balanced budget by 1998/99.

Treasurer Peter Costello announced in the government's mid-year budget review in January a revised forecast for the 1996/97 year (to June 30) underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 billion, compared with the A$5.65 billion forecast in the August budget.

With current tax and spending policies, the underlying deficit, which excludes asset sales, would fall to A$3.93 billion in 1997/98, the review said, but the government plans to tighten its finances in the May 13 budget.
The Reserve Bank eased monetary policy three times between July and December 1996, each time lowering its overnight cash rate target by 0.5 percentage points.
